elements.label: Figure 2.6
elements.description: Grouped bar chart. Y-axis: 'Net change in employment (thousands)', ranging from -3,000 to 6,000 in steps of 1,000. X-axis categories: 2010–2014 and 2015–2020. Legend: Wage worker (teal), Employer (orange), Own account worker (grey), Unpaid family worker (yellow). No values are printed on the bars. Approximate readings (thousands): 2010–2014: Wage worker ~2,200; Employer ~-600; Own account worker ~300; Unpaid family worker ~1,750. 2015–2020: Wage worker ~4,900; Employer ~-100; Own account worker ~-1,900; Unpaid family worker ~-2,350. Source: GSO, LFS. The pattern shows wage-worker employment rising sharply in 2015–2020 while own-account and unpaid family work turned negative.

elements.label: Figure 2.7
elements.description: Grouped bar chart. Y-axis: 'Net change in employment (thousands)', ranging from -4,000 to 4,000 in steps of 1,000. X-axis categories: 2010–2014 and 2015–2020. Legend: High-skill (teal), Medium-skill (orange), Low-skill (grey). No values are printed on the bars. Approximate readings (thousands): 2010–2014: High-skill ~750; Medium-skill ~980; Low-skill ~2,050. 2015–2020: High-skill ~820; Medium-skill ~2,850; Low-skill ~-3,100. Source: GSO, LFS. The pattern shows medium-skill jobs growing most in 2015–2020 while low-skill jobs shifted to a large net decline.
